title: CAS: Conformalized Agentic Search via Adaptive Retrieval and Policy Weighting

visual_explainer.question: How do calibrated evidence-set size and trajectory weighting alter search-agent training?
visual_explainer.takeaway: APS selects a variable document set from calibrated retrieval mass, while ACI downweights high-NLL trajectories; neither guarantees answer correctness.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same Search-R1-derived package with fixed top-k retrieval or without adaptive trajectory weighting.

analysis.tldr: CAS combines conformal-inspired variable evidence-set sizing with NLL-thresholded trajectory weighting. Matched ablations improve average EM, but the statistical guarantee concerns calibrated set coverage or miscoverage frequency—not correctness, hallucination freedom, or end-to-end agent reliability.
analysis.problem: Fixed top-k can over-retrieve easy questions and miss evidence for hard ones, while RL can overweight overconfident trajectories.
analysis.core_idea: Calibrate a retrieval-score mass threshold to choose 1–5 documents per search, then adapt a quantile over answer NLL to weight rollout trajectories during GRPO.
analysis.agent_loop: query → choose adaptive evidence set → reason/search up to four rounds → score answer uncertainty → weight rollout update
analysis.retrieval_design: APS changes retrieval width using calibrated E5-score mass; ACI operates during training on final-answer token NLL. These are distinct placements of adaptivity.
compared_to: Search-R1 with the same base model
Search-R2 under an unmatched closed recipe
analysis.evidence: Qwen2.5-3B full averages 0.401 versus 0.384 without ACI and 0.389 with fixed top-k. At 8B, CAS is 0.464 versus Search-R2 0.446, but the General-QA increment is only 0.001.
analysis.why_it_matters: It offers a concrete mechanism for adapting retrieval width rather than treating top-k as a global constant.
limitations: Calibration uses 239 teacher-created queries from 150 NQ/HotpotQA examples; exchangeability across evaluation datasets is untested.
Answer NLL is not evidence of factual correctness.
No seeds or confidence intervals are reported for the matched ablations.
At alpha 0.05, more documents improve general QA but collapse multi-hop performance.
Qwen3 thinking mode stops search entirely, revealing strong harness dependence.
Training/inference tokens, realized calls, latency, GPU-hours, and dollars are incomplete.
